static_traits.name: Gao Rui
static_traits.educational_background: High school graduate, planning to enter the University of Michigan this fall
static_traits.family_status: Lives with parents and one younger sibling
static_traits.social_status: Has supportive family and friends, but has not yet discussed feelings about college-preparation pressure with them
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; no similar psychological problems in the past; never received psychotherapy or counseling
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly and in an organized way, highly cooperative, positive attitude

basic_info.main_problem: I constantly feel I must use all my time to prepare for university, to the point of neglecting self-care and relieving fatigue.
basic_info.core_demands: I realized this pressure was affecting my physical and mental health, so I sought counseling, hoping to find a more balanced way to prepare for college without sacrificing self-care.

core_beliefs: I only have worth through constant effort and achievement

special_situations.event: Still faces college preparation tasks when feeling very tired
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not keep preparing, I cannot succeed in college nor become a doctor
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repressing rest needs, extending learning time, sacrificing sleep and diet to maintain high-intensity preparation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should keep preparing, cannot stop to rest

special_situations.event: When family or friends invite participation in activities or interaction
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have not devoted all my time to preparation, it means I am not working hard enough and will fail in the future
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding socializing and family activities, devoting all time to exam and college preparation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Socializing now would be irresponsible; I will fall behind and fail because of it

special_situations.event: Still planning or doing lengthy university preparation tasks before bedtime
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: As soon as I stop to rest, I will be overtaken by others and fall behind tomorrow
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Delays rest and sleep, forcing oneself to keep working to gain a sense of security
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Stopping to rest now will make me fall behind

special_situations.event: Experiencing intense guilt and anxiety when resting or relaxing
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Feeling guilty means I should not rest right now and should go back to work
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Using continued learning to ease guilt and anxiety, avoiding the unease that relaxation brings
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I feel guilty, which shows resting is wrong

core_conflict.wish: Longing for academic success and recognition, while also wanting to be allowed to rest and be accepted
core_conflict.fear: Fear of failure, being negated, and being unable to reach the goal of becoming a doctor
defense_goal: Controlling uncertainty through excessive self-demands and sustained effort, easing failure anxiety

object_relations.self_representation: A chaser/achiever who must always work hard
object_relations.object_representation: Others who may not understand and carry high expectations and judgment

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites focusing on self-care and rest, and challenging 'should' beliefs
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Experiencing attention to rest as lowering standards, possibly affecting future success
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizing efficiency and competitiveness in a rational, goal-oriented way, frequently using words like 'must/should', downplaying or skipping emotional experiences like guilt and exhaustion.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about others' (family's, society's) expectations of success or the goal of becoming a doctor
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Treats external standards as the only correct self-requirement, believing deviation means failure
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using expressions like 'everyone is like this' and 'to become a doctor you have to be like this', in a firm tone, avoiding exploration of personal needs and boundaries.

manifestations: Constrains self-choice with rigid 'shoulds' and external standards, feeling all time must be used to prepare for university
Feeling strong guilt and anxiety before choosing rest and self-care, struggling to freely set the pace
outcomes: Physical and mental exhaustion and increased stress
Relationship tension with family and friends, estrangement

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Frequently using self-demand statements like 'I should/must keep preparing'
Taking 'success = sustained high-intensity work' as an unquestionable rule

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Strong guilt about rest and relaxation; excessive self-reproach
Worrying others will think they are exaggerating or will not understand, hence not daring to express pressure to family and friends

positive_force: Excellent academic performance, with the ability for sustained effort and self-discipline
Has a supportive family and friend network
Keeps awareness of the problem and proactively seeks counseling help
Positive attitude, willing to try behavioral experiments and adjust routines
negative_force: Rigid beliefs and high expectations about success and failure ('should' thinking)
Guilt and anxiety experiences about rest and relaxation
Avoiding expressing pressure to family and friends, not yet effectively mobilizing social support
Over-investment in preparation damaging sleep and diet, interpersonal tension

target_behavior.behavior: Continuously pushes oneself on college preparation, finding it hard to rest and care for oneself
antecedent: Feeling exhausted but thinking of college and the goal of becoming a doctor
The automatic thought 'I should keep working' appears
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalized high standards and worry about failure trigger 'should'-style self-demands and predictions of falling behind
target_behavior.function: Gaining a sense of control through sustained work, easing guilt and anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Worsening fatigue and pressure, sleep and diet affected, decreased efficiency, interpersonal tension

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids discussing own stress and feelings with family and friends
antecedent: Thinking they may not understand or see the reaction as excessive
Tending to devote time to preparation tasks when feeling anxious and guilty
target_behavior.core_reason: Worry about others' judgments and avoidance of vulnerability
target_behavior.function: Escaping potential negation and conflict, briefly lowering social anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Social support not yet effectively mobilized, emotional pressure internalized, interpersonal alienation
